items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell 1.03% to 7,341 Tuesday, its lowest close since late July, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.74% to 24,328, a third straight loss.
items.why: Investors cut risk before Nvidia's results and Anthropic's IPO, with a December Fed hike priced at about 95%.

items.detail: **Nvidia** posted record revenue of **$115.8 billion**, up 103%, and guided to about $130 billion, lifting the stock roughly 4% after hours from $155.46.
items.why: Data-center sales of $107.6 billion showed AI demand holding up despite Jensen Huang's exit.

items.detail: Anthropic's IPO debuts today at a valuation of up to **$1.4 trillion**, the next test of whether Nvidia's beat can revive AI appetite.
Korea's **Kospi** jumped **2.62%** to 5,098.54 Wednesday, snapping a four-day losing streak, as SK Hynix rose about 5% and Samsung nearly 4%.
items.why: Nvidia's strong results and outlook eased fears about AI chip demand and slowed foreign selling of Korean chipmakers.

items.detail: India's two-day rally stalled: the **Sensex** fell about 300 points in early trade Wednesday from 82,532, with metal stocks like NALCO and SAIL leading losses.
items.why: Weak Asian cues, rising US Treasury yields and Middle East tensions outweighed Nvidia's upbeat results.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell about **1.5%** Tuesday, lagging the S&P 500 as small caps took the brunt of the selloff.
items.why: A 10-year yield near 5.1% raises borrowing costs for smaller, debt-reliant companies.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** slipped back below **$64,000** Tuesday and barely moved after Nvidia's record quarter, with support seen near $61,000 to $62,100.
items.why: The tech selloff and near-certain Fed hike bets kept risk appetite thin, so Nvidia's beat did not spill over.

items.detail: **Ether** fell 2.7% to about **$1,775**, sliding further below last week's $1,850 level.
items.why: It tracked bitcoin lower as the stock selloff and a strong dollar kept buyers away.

items.detail: **Solana** held near **$72**, the only top-10 token in the green Tuesday, though it is still down about 27% over the past month.
items.why: Buyers kept defending the weekend's four-month low, even as the wider crypto market stayed weak.

items.detail: **Gold** fell 1.4% to **$3,796.37** Wednesday, breaking below $3,800 for its lowest level since September 2025 and wiping out Tuesday's bounce.
items.why: The dollar sits near a 19-month high and Fed officials are signaling more rate hikes.

crossCuttingTheme: Nvidia's record quarter lifted Asian chipmakers, but a dollar near a 19-month high and an almost certain December Fed hike kept pushing gold, crypto and US small caps lower.
